title: Equivalent Ratios: Scaling and Unit Rate
preview: An 8-step thin-slice that takes one ratio (3 cups : 2 servings) and scales it up, down, and to a unit rate one variation at a time.

body.goal: Students see scaling and unit rate as one move (multiply both quantities by the same factor), not two separate procedures.
body.launch: Tell the story (the stem above stays on the screen): 'A pancake recipe uses 3 cups of mix to make 2 servings.' Don't draw a table — let groups invent their own representations.
body.stem: A pancake recipe uses 3 cups of mix to make 2 servings.

steps.teacherNote: Pause. 'What are you doing each time?' Multiplication by the same factor should surface.
First non-whole answer. Some groups will reach for fractions, some decimals — let both stand.
Watch for groups using their unit rate (1.5 × 5).
Direction reversed. Some groups freeze — push them: 'You found cups → servings. Now servings ← cups.'
The other unit rate. Now both unit rates are on the board.
Choose your weapon — most groups will pick whichever unit rate fits.

body.consolidation: Ask: 'What did every problem have in common?' Push for the idea: scaling = multiply both numbers by the same factor; unit rate is just one specific scaling.
